checkpoints.title: Small and reliable
checkpoints.narration: It scales to whatever GPUs are available with distributed data parallelism. It's merely two thousand lines, so it's easy to debug in production. The tests give very strong quality guarantees, so it just works: we trained a swarm with TorchTitan and with this job and compared them. And it's fully self-contained, eval suite included, so it's reliable to ship with no silent drift.

checkpoints.title: What BPB measures
checkpoints.narration: Evaluation asks how well the model predicts a continuation after reading its context. Take a toy continuation: the letter A, one UTF-8 byte. If the model gives its token probability one quarter, that costs two bits: minus log base two of one quarter. Two bits divided by one byte gives two bits per byte. Across a longer continuation, add the prediction bits and divide by its bytes. Lower is better.
checkpoints.visual: Show context “Next letter:” in the context color and continuation “A” in the continuation color. This toy tokenizer emits A as one token. Carry p(A)=0.25 into −log₂(0.25)=2 bits, and the actual UTF-8 byte 0x41 into a one-byte denominator. Resolve 2 bits / 1 byte = 2 BPB. Keep context bytes and context predictions outside both accumulators; then fan out to longer pairs.
checkpoints.notes: The numerical example is deliberately constructed, not a measured model prediction; A is one token in the toy and one UTF-8 byte. General BPB is negative summed natural-log likelihood divided by ln(2) and continuation UTF-8 bytes. Per-task result is mean document BPB, not a byte-weighted aggregate.

checkpoints.title: A curve, not one score
checkpoints.narration: We do this across thousands of pairs, at checkpoints during training and once more at the end. Each evaluation gives another point on the learning curve.
checkpoints.visual: Show training segments interrupted by small evaluation segments. Each evaluation emits a point into a BPB-versus-training-tokens curve. Hold the final curve, with no invented numerical y-values.
checkpoints.notes: Mid-training sample evaluation defaults to every 500 steps and up to 50 documents per task; full evaluation follows the final step. The curve is schematic unless actual source scores are supplied.

slides.title: Optimization 2: Custom training kernels
slides.transition: The counter stays at the top right; the title is fixed.

checkpoints.title: Normal flow
checkpoints.narration: Normally the LM head writes logits for the whole microbatch, cross-entropy reads them back to compute the loss, and calling backward makes PyTorch compute the logit gradients and then the two matmuls for dH and dW.
checkpoints.visual: Left: the four steps of the normal flow, GPU steps as purple rectangles and CPU steps as yellow circles.
screen: gpu|GPU · forward|LM-head matmul writes the full microbatch of logits
gpu|GPU · forward|Cross-entropy reads the logits and computes the loss
gpu|GPU · backward|PyTorch computes the logit gradients, then two matmuls give dH and dW

checkpoints.title: QuACK base flow
checkpoints.narration: QuACK loops over token chunks. For each chunk it computes the logits, computes the loss while overwriting those logits with their gradients, and runs the dH matmul and most of the dW matmuls. Backward then only scales the prepared gradients and finishes the last dW matmul.
checkpoints.visual: Right: the four steps of the QuACK base flow beside the normal flow.
screen: cpu|CPU orchestration|Loop over token chunks and launch the GPU work
gpu|GPU · QuACK forward|Per chunk: compute logits; compute the loss and overwrite the logits with their gradients; run the dH matmul and most dW matmuls
gpu|GPU · QuACK backward|Scale the prepared gradients and finish the last dW matmul

checkpoints.title: The costs
checkpoints.narration: This is expensive and inflexible. CPU scheduling clogs the swarm, every model pays GPU hours for repeated overhead, it only fits fixed-capacity clusters, it can't burst, and a claimed GPU can't be reused without scheduling again.

checkpoints.title: A queue and warm workers
checkpoints.narration: In the new workflow, one CPU fills a task queue with many tasks, and a stack of warm, cache-reuse workers pulls from it. Finished train checkpoints and evals land on the right.

checkpoints.title: Async CPU threads
checkpoints.narration: Every non-GPU step, like exporting and uploading checkpoints, runs on asynchronous CPU threads, so the GPU keeps training.
